0c8012.title: Ilocano Teatro repository architecture map
0c8012.content:
## Runtime product

- Flutter/Dart client: `lib/` (58 Dart files, ~19,191 LOC).
- Entry point: `lib/main.dart`; initializes Supabase from compile-time `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` and runs `TeatroApp`.
- App/Auth: `lib/app/**`, `lib/features/auth/**`, `lib/features/shell/**`.
- Feature modules: auth, dashboard, drafts/theme submissions, learning/progress, notifications, profile/class assignment, quiz, story vault, and teacher review/curriculum/student-progress.
- Backend authority: bootstrap SQL `ilocano_teatro_master_supabase_setup.sql`, 11 migrations under `supabase/migrations/`, and Deno Edge Function `supabase/functions/get-private-media/index.ts`.
- Android package/config: `android/`; manifest requests Internet permission.

## Non-runtime/development boundaries

- `test/`: 30 Flutter/Dart tests.
- `supabase/diagnostics/`: read-only/cleanup diagnostic SQL.
- `docs/`, `state/`: readiness and working-state documentation.
- `design_reference/`: Figma/reference source with its own `AGENTS.md`; not imported by product Dart code.
- `build/`, `.dart_tool/`, `android/.gradle/`: generated caches/artifacts.
- `.qa-test-accounts.local.json`, `.env`, `supabase.local.json`: local configuration/QA material; secrets inventory is being handled by scanner output.

## Trust boundary

The Flutter client talks directly to Supabase Auth/PostgREST/RPC/Storage. UI role routing is not authoritative; RLS, SQL functions, storage policies, and the private-media Edge Function are the security boundary. The Edge Function may use service-role access only after caller authentication and authorization.

4d7bbd.title: Ilocano Teatro route, role, and data inventory
4d7bbd.content:
## Roles and routes

`AuthGate` resolves `profiles.role` to `student` or `teacher`. `AppDestination` defines: `/dashboard`, `/learning`, `/module/:id`, `/lesson/:id`, `/quiz/:id`, `/story-vault`, `/story/:id`, `/story-chapter`, `/story-editor`, `/story-chapter-editor`, `/theme-builder`, `/drafts`, `/progress`, `/review-queue`, `/submission/:id`, `/student-progress`, `/learning-content`, `/notifications`, and `/profile`. Named auth routes include `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, and `/forgot-password`.

Student navigation includes dashboard, learning/module/lesson/quiz, story vault/readers, theme builder/drafts/progress, notifications, and profile. Teacher navigation includes dashboard, review queue/submission review, student progress, story vault/editors, learning-content/curriculum management, quiz management, notifications, and profile. These are client-side navigation decisions only.

## Data model

Tables observed across bootstrap/migrations: `profiles`, `teacher_students`, `learning_modules`, `lessons`, `lesson_progress`, `quizzes`, `quiz_questions`, `question_options`, `quiz_attempts`, `quiz_answers`, `theme_drafts`, `submissions`, `rubric_criteria`, `reviews`, `review_scores`, `notifications`, `cultural_stories`, `story_chapters`, `story_reading_progress`, `curriculum_editors`, and `teacher_class_codes`.

Client repositories reference 18 of these tables and RPCs `create_class_join_code`, `get_active_class_join_code`, `get_my_teacher_connection`, `is_curriculum_editor`, and `revoke_class_join_code`; additional mutations are protected by database functions/triggers. The SQL corpus has 22 RLS enables, 58 policy declarations, and 23 `SECURITY DEFINER` occurrences. Exact call-site inventory is preserved in `/workspace/.source-aware-ilocano/client-data-map.txt` and SQL map in `/workspace/.source-aware-ilocano/sql-security-map.txt`.

## File/outbound/parser surfaces

Local image bytes enter through `file_picker` and client validators for avatars/story media. Private media retrieval uses a fixed Supabase Edge Function endpoint derived from the configured Supabase REST URL. No general attacker-selected outbound URL, process execution, shell, XML parser, or native filesystem sink was found in runtime Dart code. Stored lessons/stories/quizzes use structured Dart models and Flutter widgets rather than a browser HTML/WebView surface.

1c47f6.title: Ilocano Teatro dependency and scanner inventory
1c47f6.content:
## Direct dependencies

`pubspec.yaml` directly declares Flutter SDK, `cupertino_icons ^2.0.0`, `supabase_flutter ^2.18.3`, `file_picker ^13.3.0`, `http ^1.6.0`, and `web ^1.1.2`; `flutter_test` and `flutter_lints ^6.0.0` are development dependencies. `pubspec.lock` is present. The private-media Deno Edge Function imports the floating major specifier `npm:@supabase/supabase-js@2`.

## Scanner artifact directory and results

Concise artifacts are under `/workspace/.source-aware-ilocano/`:

- `semgrep.json`: `p/default` plus `p/secrets`, scoped to runtime/config source; 78 files scanned, 0 findings, 0 engine errors.
- `sg-targets.txt`: derived from Semgrep `paths.scanned`; `ast-grep.json` contains 113 bounded structural call records, with no AST engine errors.
- `gitleaks.json`: targeted worktree pass over product source, backend source, manifests, lockfiles, and local config; 3 generic-key detections, limited to ignored `.env` (2) and ignored `supabase.local.json` (1). No detections in `lib/`, `supabase/`, Android manifest, pubspec, or QA-account JSON.
- `gitleaks-history.json`: full reachable Git-history pass; 0 detector hits. A separate redacted object-structure check was required because the historical QA passwords did not match a Gitleaks rule; see note `836cf3`.
- `trufflehog.json`: empty; the attempted complementary invocation did not produce usable results, so Gitleaks plus Semgrep secrets are the completed secrets coverage.
- `trivy-fs.json`: 2 result targets, 0 known dependency vulnerabilities and 0 misconfigurations, with generated/cache directories excluded.

No dynamic credential validation was performed, consistent with the static-only constraint.

836cf3.title: Historical QA credential candidate ruled out as agent-checkpoint artifact
836cf3.content:
Counterevidence review disproved repository-history exposure.

The credential-bearing object appears only in commit `02cd4ee5cbc57b191eca38e79a2c7339218d0d0d`, whose subject identifies an agent-host checkpoint. Its deletion commit `77f2ff4db6ee87cb3137eb04fa742742b27abfb3` is the immediately following checkpoint. Both commits are reachable exclusively from `refs/agents/<id>/checkpoints/...`; neither is an ancestor of `HEAD`, and neither is contained by any of the 11 local branch refs, 12 remote-tracking refs, or tags. The repository has a configured GitHub origin, but no shared ref contains the object. Available metadata therefore shows the commits were created by the local assistant checkpoint mechanism, not by the project's branch history or remote.

The current `.qa-test-accounts.local.json` is untracked and ignored by `.gitignore`; its historic checkpoint content matches the current ignored file. The values are plausible live QA accounts rather than obvious reserved-domain fixtures: role-labeled addresses use a non-reserved domain, the passwords are nonempty, the configured target is a hosted Supabase project, and `docs/CLIENT_TESTING_READINESS_2026-11-03.md` states the dedicated accounts authenticated successfully. No live service was contacted and no value was disclosed.

Because the only Git object containing the file was generated by internal checkpoint refs and never entered a project/shared ref, there is no source-repository credential exposure to report. The correct closure is **ruled out**. Local credential rotation remains optional operational hygiene, not remediation for a demonstrated repository leak.

16d5e6.title: Supabase authorization audit closure
16d5e6.content:
Completed static review of all 58 `CREATE POLICY` statements, all application-table grants/revokes, and every `SECURITY DEFINER` function in the bootstrap/migrations. Artifacts: `/workspace/.source-aware-ilocano/all-policies.txt` and `/workspace/.source-aware-ilocano/definer-audit.txt`.

Controls confirmed:

- All 21 application tables enable RLS. `profiles.role` defaults to `student`, the signup trigger ignores user-supplied role metadata, and authenticated users receive column-level profile UPDATE only for non-role fields.
- `is_teacher`, `can_review`, and `is_curriculum_editor` bind checks to `auth.uid()`; editor assignment tables have no client grants.
- Privileged submission, review, quiz, reorder, answer-key, and class-code functions use `search_path = ''`, explicit role/ownership/assignment checks, and public/anon revokes. Trigger functions are non-callable outside trigger context or have EXECUTE revoked.
- Class join codes are 128-bit random, hashed for lookup, time-bounded/revocable, limited to student callers, and serialized by a one-teacher-per-student unique index.
- Quiz answers/attempts and theme submissions/reviews are written only through trusted functions; direct authenticated writes are revoked.
- Story/profile Storage policies bind bucket, operation, path shape, role/ownership, and referenced record state.

Counterchecked candidates:

1. `scores_read` looks broad because it only tests for a matching `reviews` row. It is ruled out: the subquery executes as the authenticated query user and `reviews_read` RLS restricts visible review rows to the owning student or assigned teacher; no security-definer wrapper bypasses that RLS.
2. `questions_read`/`options_read` do not repeat `is_published`. They are ruled out by transitive RLS: `questions_read` can only see a `quizzes` row allowed by `quizzes_read` (published quiz and published module), and `options_read` can only see a question allowed by `questions_read`. The quiz migration additionally restricts columns so learners cannot select `explanation` or `is_correct`.
3. UI role routing can be bypassed, but every privileged backend path is independently enforced by RLS/RPC checks, so it is not an authorization finding.

No complete static authorization vulnerability was confirmed. No report was filed.
